title: IELTS Listening Practice - Listening - Social Media Influencers in Politics
subject: Listening

questions.q:
### Context: How are influencers affecting politics? - 6 Minute English

**Watch the video (or listen to the audio context provided) and answer Questions 1-10.**

![How are influencers affecting politics?](https://img.youtube.com/vi/Pej48NfVg2I/mqdefault.jpg)
[Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pej48NfVg2I&t=64s)

**Questions 1–4**
Choose the correct letter, **a**, **b**, or **c**.

1. What is the primary activity of social media influencers mentioned at the start of the discussion?
questions.explain: Pippa states: 'These social media influencers do what they’re famous for: influencing and creating trends.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 2. Which group has recently started paying close attention to the success of influencers?
questions.explain: Pippa mentions that the success of influencers has 'caught the attention of another group... politicians.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 3. In which countries have there been allegations of politicians paying for influencer support?
questions.explain: Pippa lists the countries: 'There have even been allegations of politicians paying for the support of influencers in places like Colombia, Argentina, and Indonesia.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 4. Why is Nigeria specifically mentioned in the context of social media and politics?
options: It has the highest number of internet users in Africa.
It has a very large and young population.
It has banned political advertising on TV.
questions.explain: Pippa explains: 'Nigeria is a country with a huge, young population. There are around 200 million people... and 70% of them are under 30.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q:
**Questions 5–10**
Complete the sentences below. Write **NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS** for each answer.

5. Many young voters in Nigeria are described as being '______' by traditional media.
questions.explain: The text states: 'Many of these young voters are turned off, meaning not interested, in traditional media.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 6. Adeline Okere believes influencers are super important for shaping the ______ of elections.
questions.explain: Adeline says: 'Influencers are super important to shaping the narrative of these young people.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 7. Some influencers began their careers in ______ or lifestyle content before moving into politics.
questions.explain: Adeline mentions: 'Some of them started in, you know, activism. Some of them started out with lifestyle...'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 8. When an influencer moves into a new area like politics, they are said to be ______ out.
questions.explain: Adeline says: '...and then branched into politics.' Beth later defines 'branching out'.
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 9. In Nigeria, there was a huge ______ against influencers who promoted political parties.
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 10. The public reaction involved finding and publishing information from the influencers' ______ lives.
questions.explain: Adeline states: '...dig up information about these people from their personal lives...'
questions.subject: Listening
